subject: Post-call: SierraHealth integration & routing policy checklist
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sierrahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan.li@sierrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call follow-up / technical notes

Thanks for the call today — the team found the demo helpful. A few clarifications from our side to help scope the POC: 

1) Traffic profile: expect 5–10 concurrent inference sessions during pilot, bursts up to ~50 QPS for short windows. Average prompt length ~120 tokens, responses ~160 tokens.
2) Data handling: PHI will be present in prompts; we need to understand where data is stored, retention by default, and whether we can turn off training/usage logging for the pilot.
3) Auth: currently we prefer mTLS for the private deployment but are open to short-lived API keys for hosted.
4) Integrations: we'll need embeddings for semantic search and a lightweight reranker for top-K results; tool calling for structured extraction (JSON output) is also critical.

Can you send a short checklist of SDK/auth steps, recommended routing profiles (latency vs cost), and the fallback chain you suggested on the call? Also attach the diagram you referenced.

Best,
Alex
Sierra Health — Director of Data Products

---

(Attachment: sierra-mvp-arch.pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sierrahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T17:02:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call: SierraHealth integration & routing policy checklist

Alex — thanks for the detailed notes, appreciated. Recap + concrete next steps below.

Quick answers to the bullets you raised:
- Traffic: pilot sizing looks good — we'll configure an autoscaling headroom for bursts to 60 QPS and monitor.
- Data handling: hosted API defaults to no training; we'll enable a Data Processing Agreement option and can offer "no retention" flag for the pilot. For Private (VPC), logs are customer-controlled.
- Auth: we support both mTLS (private) and short-lived API keys with federated token exchange for hosted.
- Embeddings/reranker/tooling: recommend separate embedding index service + a small-reranker model to cut down rerank cost. We can show latency/cost tradeoffs below.

Action items (we own items 1–3; your team owns 4–5):
1) Redwood: deliver a one-page SDK quickstart (node/python) showing auth, streaming, and structured output examples (ETA: 2026-10-07).
2) Redwood: attach routing profiles CSV with suggested latency/cost thresholds and fallback chains. (Attachment: redwood-routing-profiles.csv)
3) Redwood: provide a minimal config for embeddings + reranker pipeline (which model to host where, expected per-request token cost) — attaching recommended mapping.
4) Sierra: confirm retention policy for pilot and who owns KMS for Private deploy.
5) Sierra: provide a sample prompt/response pair and expected SLAs (p95 latency target).
6) Schedule: propose a 30–45m technical POC session next week to walk through SDK and live routing tests.

Routing recommendation (summary):
- Region routing: route US patient-facing traffic to us-east to minimize egress. EU traffic (if any) should be pinned to eu-west.
- Latency-first profile: for p95 < 200ms use the low-latency variant (quantized FP16 optimized) on dedicated capacity; fallback chain = low-latency -> default FP16 -> cost-optimized int8.
- Cost-first profile: for batch/embeddings workloads route to cost-optimized int8 pools with higher batching windows.
- Fallbacks: define a hard-fail fallback to a smaller domain-specialized model rather than returning 5xx.

I'll attach the quickstart + routing CSV in a follow-up. If this looks good, let's lock the POC slot for Tue 2026-10-13 or Wed 2026-10-14.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
---
(Attachment: redwood-routing-profiles.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sierrahealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:11:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SierraHealth integration & routing policy checklist

Alex — quick technical notes to prep for the POC session: 

SDK & Auth (quickstart highlights)
- Node/Python SDKs include a config object: {api_key, region, routing_profile}. For hosted tests use short-lived tokens; for Private we'll provide instructions for client certs (mTLS).
- Example structured-output call (pseudo):
  - request: {prompt, tool_call: {schema: patient_summary_v1}}
  - response: {json: {...}, content: "..."} — SDK will validate schema when using function/tool calls.

Model routing & policies
- Policy primitives: latency_threshold_ms, cost_per_token_usd, allowed_models, region_preference, fallback_chain (ordered).
- Example latency-first policy: {latency_threshold_ms:200, allowed_models:[rwd-lowlatency-v1, rwd-fp16-v2], fallback_chain:[rwd-fp16-v2, rwd-int8-cost]}
- Embeddings: put embeddings index in same region as inference to avoid egress; batch embeddings in windows of 250–500 vectors for cost efficiency. Reranker: host a mid-size model (rwd-ranker-v1) on dedicated pool; sequence length cap at 512 to control cost.

Operational checks for POC
- Confirm sample QPS and p95 target (Alex).
- Provide a short-lived API key and example curl + SDK snippet for Sierra to hit the hosted endpoint.
- We'll run a 15-minute latency sweep from Sierra's office IPs during POC to validate routing decisions.

I'll drop the quickstart snippets into the shared Drive folder today.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few quick answers from the security side before we schedule: 

- Retention: for the pilot we want no retention and all logs forwarded to our SIEM. Please confirm hosted option supports a no-retain flag per request.
- KMS: for Private we will provide a customer-managed KMS; for hosted we'll require envelope encryption with our key in KMS where possible.
- mTLS: happy to do the cert exchange during POC, but would like a short checklist of required cert fields and allowed CAs.

Next steps from Sierra (we'll do 1–3):
1) Confirmed: sample prompt/response and p95 target = 180ms.
2) We'll share office IPs and a minimal dataset (redacted) for embeddings index by EOD 10/08.
3) Confirmed POC slot: Tue 2026-10-13 10:00 AM ET works for our infra lead.

Look forward to the SDK snippets and routing CSV.

Jordan Li
Senior Engineer, Data Platforms — Sierra Health
